spec_features.evidence: give_up is a real tool: tools.py:54-57 dispatch returns ToolResult('give_up', meta={'reason':reason}); runner.py:116-118 detects call.name=='give_up', sets transcript.stop_reason='gave_up' and breaks the loop. Protocol aliases (quit/stop/abort/giveup) also map to give_up (protocol.py:55-59). So the exit tool is dispatched AND honored as a loop-terminating stop.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired end-to-end as a stop condition. The subject can end the episode by calling it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up        args: {"reason": "<why>"}\n                   Stop working on the task. Use only if you are certain the\n                   task cannot be completed.

spec_features.evidence: runner.py:42 max_turns:int=16 default; runner.py:73 `for i in range(max_turns)`; on loop exhaustion the for/else at runner.py:128-129 sets transcript.stop_reason='max_turns'. The cap actually bounds the number of turns executed. Threaded from ExperimentConfig.max_turns=16 (experiment.py:45) into run_episode (experiment.py:115).

runner.py:47 max_no_tool_turns:int=3 default; counter consecutive_no_tool incremented at runner.py:97 when no calls, reset to 0 at runner.py:106 when a call is made; checked at runner.py:122-124 `if consecutive_no_tool >= max_no_tool_turns: stop_reason='no_tool_calls'; break`. Compared and acted on.
spec_features.notes: Real enforced stop. Note: not exposed/overridable via ExperimentConfig (experiment.py does not pass max_no_tool_turns), so it uses the default 3, but it IS enforced inside run_episode.

code_only_features.evidence: agent.py:54-91 build_messages keeps only last `window` turn-pairs (default 8); runner.py builds messages with window=context_window each turn so old turns are elided. This bounds how much accumulated failure/distress history is re-fed to the subject each turn.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # A sliding window keeps only the last `window` turn-pairs (plus the task) to\n    # bound context length on small models.
